entries.subject: Sicardy et al. (2011) 2010 stellar-occultation radius
entries.finding: The render sphere uses the nominal 1,163 ± 6 km radius from the 6 November 2010 occultation, which the README says is consistent with a spherical body and is not a claim of a resolved shape mesh.

entries.subject: Shared neutral gray for the unresolved surface
entries.finding: Replaced by the measured whole-disc colour. The gray was a display convention; published colour indices and a V geometric albedo now give Eris a measured uniform colour, which the shape-only convention does not supersede.
entries.revisitWhen: The published colour or albedo is withdrawn or shown not to describe the whole disc.

entries.subject: Disc-resolved images of Eris
entries.finding: No usable resolved image exists. At about 96 AU the 2,326 km disc spans about 0.034 arcsec (computed from the occultation radius), about two diffraction widths of an 8 m telescope at 650 nm (0.016 arcsec); VLT/SPHERE frames of rounder bodies with far larger discs were already undecidable. No spacecraft has visited.
entries.revisitWhen: A disc-resolved image, a 30 m class telescope observation or a flyby is published.

entries.subject: Carraro et al. (2006) BVRI colours
entries.finding: B-V 0.823 +/-0.023, V-R 0.391 +/-0.023, V-I 0.777 +/-0.013 (section 4, weighted means over five nights in 2005; V-R stable night to night) give the uniform Color lens through the disc-integrated-color method.

entries.subject: Sicardy et al. (2011) V geometric albedo
entries.finding: p_V 0.96 +0.09/-0.04 from the 2010 occultation radius scales the colour; the same value was already pinned in measurements.json.

entries.subject: MBOSS mean colours
entries.finding: The MBOSS catalogue (J/A+A/546/A115) averages 64 epochs from Carraro et al. (2006), DeMeo et al. (2009) and Rabinowitz et al. (2007): B-V 0.805 +/-0.015, V-R 0.389 +/-0.049, V-I 0.792 +/-0.018. Measured with the same method and albedo, it gives sRGB 255, 250, 236 against 255, 250, 234 from Carraro; the single-run set is kept because its V-R is better constrained.
entries.revisitWhen: A newer multi-epoch colour set disagrees with Carraro et al. (2006) beyond their uncertainties.

entries.subject: Colour at the top of the sRGB range
entries.finding: The nominal colour is linear sRGB 0.999, 0.952, 0.827. Measured with the same method: B-V +0.023, V-R +0.023 or an albedo of 1.00 put red above 1, and the method refuses the colour. B-V -0.023 gives 255, 250, 237; V-R -0.023 gives 253, 249, 235; the albedo's lower bound 0.92 gives 250, 245, 230.
entries.revisitWhen: The colour or albedo is revised, or the shared method gains a stated rule for colours brighter than sRGB white.

entries.subject: Dysnomia light in the photometry
entries.finding: Carraro et al. (2006) state that the unresolved moon Dysnomia may contribute about 0.02 mag to the total brightness. The colours include it; the occultation albedo does not. No correction is applied.
entries.revisitWhen: Published colours that separate Eris from Dysnomia.

entries.subject: Bernstein et al. (2023) photometric rotation period
entries.finding: Rotation content states the 15.771 ± 0.008-day photometric period, consistent with synchronous rotation at Dysnomia's 15.78590-day orbital period; the README notes the period is content only and drives no absolute rotational ephemeris.

entries.subject: NASA overview 25.9-hour rotation period
entries.finding: The README records that the adopted 15.771-day period supersedes the 25.9-hour value still present on NASA's overview page, so that value is not used.
entries.revisitWhen: A new published determination reinstates a sub-day rotation period for Eris.

entries.subject: Vendored JPL elements for the scene position
entries.finding: The existing vendored JPL elements determine Eris's orbital position at the shared preparation epoch, as recorded under known problems.

entries.subject: Spin-pole and prime-meridian registration
entries.finding: Known problems record that Eris has no measured longitude origin and no established spin-pole registration, so the display pole and meridian are explicitly arbitrary.
entries.revisitWhen: A published pole solution or longitude system for Eris allows the displayed orientation to be registered.

entries.subject: NASA VTAD Eris 3D model texture as an illustration lens
entries.finding: Shown as the non-default Illustration lens, never as imagery: NASA's artist texture carried through the model's own UVs, unrepainted, with arbitrary longitudes. No image resolves Eris, so nothing in it was observed. Removed in #238 when the neutral gray replaced it; restored beside the measured Color lens, which stays the default.

entries.subject: Scene position source
entries.finding: Eris is placed from the direct JPL Horizons geometric state at the fixed scene epoch, retained in its moon's package as dysnomia/source/orbit/eris-epoch.txt, instead of from propagating its own osculating elements. This is the existing pattern for a parent with a moon: Haumea is placed from hiiaka/source/orbit/haumea-epoch.txt and Sylvia from romulus/source/orbit/sylvia-heliocentric.txt. Eris keeps its own dwarfPlanet element block for its orbit line. The change moved Eris by 92,802 km, 6.5e-6 of its 95.465 au heliocentric distance and about 1.3 arcsec seen from the Sun. The earlier elements osculate at JD 2461041.5 and were propagated 245 days; the direct state needs no propagation. Shape, size, material, lenses, text and datasets are unchanged.
